lessons.title: Evidentiality and the Subjunctive
lessons.learn: Calibrate certainty by distinguishing reported fact, inference, and evaluation.

grammar.title: Mood after stance expressions
grammar.explain: Indicative mood presents information as asserted; the subjunctive after no parece que, es posible que, and evaluative frames suspends or evaluates commitment. The choice is semantic, not decorative.

lessons.title: Cohesion, Reference, and Reported Discourse
lessons.learn: Build extended arguments whose references, reported voices, concessions, and consequences remain unambiguous.

grammar.title: Cohesive reference and sequence
grammar.explain: C1 discourse uses lexical reference, demonstratives, and reported speech to avoid both mechanical repetition and vague pronouns. Connectors must encode a real relation between propositions.

lessons.title: Atribución sin aval: al parecer, presuntamente, según fuentes
lessons.learn: Spanish distances a claim with adverbs and frames: AL PARECER, PRESUNTAMENTE, AL PARECER QUE, SEGÚN FUENTES, AL PARECER HABRÍA. The frame says who owns the claim — and the conditional keeps it a report.

grammar.title: Evidential frames
grammar.pattern: al parecer + indicative · al parecer, habría + participle · presuntamente + fact
grammar.explain: Al parecer, el ministro habría dimitido. Presuntamente se pagaron comisiones. The conditional (habría dimitido) labels the news as unconfirmed — dropping it turns the sentence into an assertion.

examples.t: Al parecer, el ministro habría dimitido.
examples.r: al pah-reh-SEHR, el mee-NEES-troh ah-BREE-ah dee-mee-TEE-doh.
examples.en: Apparently the minister has stepped down.

examples.t: Presuntamente se pagaron comisiones.
examples.r: preh-soon-tah-MEN-teh seh pah-GAH-rohn koh-mee-SYOH-nehs.
examples.en: Commissions were allegedly paid.

examples.t: Según fuentes del partido, habrá elecciones.
examples.r: seh-GOON FWEHN-tehs del par-TEE-doh, ah-BRAH eh-lek-SYOH-nehs.
examples.en: According to party sources, there will be elections.

mistakes.right: Al parecer, el ministro habría dimitido.

mistakes.why: One evidential per claim; certainty cancels the hedge.

dialogue.en: No. Apparently he has resigned — two sources, none official.

dialogue.t: ¿Y el titular?

dialogue.en: 'Apparently the minister has stepped down' — with the attribution inside it.

lessons.title: Professional Diplomacy and Mitigated Requests
lessons.learn: Negotiate deadlines, disagreement, and responsibility without obscuring the requested action.

grammar.title: Conditional mitigation
grammar.explain: The conditional and imperfect subjunctive can soften proposals and requests. Mitigation protects rapport, but an effective professional message still names the action, actor, and deadline.

lessons.title: Academic Definition and Qualified Comparison
lessons.learn: Define analytical terms, compare equivalent evidence, and preserve scope in reformulation.

grammar.title: Qualification and nominalisation
grammar.explain: Academic Spanish often packages processes as nouns, but nominalisation must not hide the agent or inflate certainty. A comparison states population, criterion, and limitation.

examples.t: La conclusión se limita a la muestra urbana estudiada.
examples.r: la konklusion se limita a la muestra urbana estudyada
examples.en: The conclusion is limited to the urban sample studied.

examples.t: La correlación observada no demuestra por sí sola causalidad.
examples.r: la korrelasion observada no demuestra por si sola kausalidad
examples.en: The observed correlation does not by itself demonstrate causality.

examples.t: En otras palabras, aumentó el promedio, no cada uno de los valores.
examples.r: en otras palabras aumento el promedyo no kada uno de los valores

lessons.title: Causalidad graduada: contribuye a, podría explicar, apunta a que
lessons.learn: Careful Spanish causal prose grades the link: CONTRIBUYE A (contributes), PODRÍA EXPLICAR (may explain), APUNTA A QUE (points to), NO BASTA PARA (is not enough to). Each verb states how strong the link is.

grammar.title: Calibrated cause
grammar.pattern: contribuye a · podría explicar · apunta a que · no basta para
grammar.explain: La demanda contribuye al aumento, pero no basta para explicarlo. The sentence holds a mechanism and its limit in one clause pair — the signature of Spanish academic prose.

examples.en: The data points to the market recovering.

examples.r: OO-nah koh-rreh-lah-SYOHN noh BAHS-tah PAH-rah ah-feer-MAR OO-nah KOW-sah.
examples.en: A correlation is not enough to assert a cause.

lessons.title: Source Synthesis and Public Mediation
lessons.learn: Synthesize conflicting sources and explain technical conclusions to a non-specialist audience without distorting certainty.

grammar.title: Concession and mediation
grammar.explain: A synthesis relates sources rather than listing them. Public mediation retains the proposition and evidence limits while changing density, terminology, and examples for the audience.
grammar.pattern: source A + relation to source B + warranted synthesis

lessons.title: Síntesis: dos fuentes en un párrafo
lessons.learn: Synthesis names the sources and then speaks with one voice: SEGÚN EL INSTITUTO …, LA PATRONAL SEÑALA POR SU LADO … — EN LO QUE AMBAS COINCIDEN ES EN QUE … The third sentence is the synthesis.

grammar.title: Source sandwich
grammar.pattern: según A … · B señala por su lado … · en lo que ambos coinciden es en que …
grammar.explain: Según el instituto, la cifra es estable. La patronal señala por su lado riesgos. En lo que ambos coinciden es en que faltan datos. Three sentences, two positions, one honest conclusion.

examples.t: Según el instituto, la cifra es estable.
examples.r: seh-GOON el een-stee-TOO-toh, lah SEE-frah es es-TAH-bleh.
examples.en: According to the institute the figure is stable.

examples.t: La patronal señala riesgos por su lado.
examples.r: lah pah-troh-NAL seh-NYAH-lah RYEH-sgohs por soo LAH-doh.
examples.en: The employers' association points to risks on its side.

examples.t: En lo que ambos coinciden es en que faltan datos.
examples.r: en loh keh AHM-bohs koh-een-SEE-dehn es en keh FAHL-tahn DAH-tohs.
examples.en: What both agree on is that data is missing.

mistakes.wrong: Ambos dicen lo mismo, pero lo contrario.
mistakes.right: Ambos ven cosas distintas y coinciden en el diagnóstico.
mistakes.why: A synthesis states difference and shared ground; it cannot merge them.
The shared point is a clause, not a noun phrase.

culture.text: Spanish bureaucratic prose runs on the passive-reflexive and on nominalisation: «se procederá a la revisión de las solicitudes presentadas en plazo». It is not decoration; it is how the administration compresses a procedure into something that can be referenced later. C1 is the level where you learn to read it without parsing twice — and to rewrite it as a sentence with a subject when a human has to act on it.

reading.text: «Se procederá a la revisión de las solicitudes presentadas en plazo», dice la resolución. La frase contiene dos acciones dentro de dos sustantivos y ningún responsable. Quien la traduce a lenguaje claro escribe: «Vamos a revisar las solicitudes que llegaron a tiempo.» El mismo contenido, un tercio de las palabras y un sujeto. Esa traducción es el trabajo de C1.
reading.gloss: 'The review of applications submitted on time will be proceeded with,' says the resolution. The sentence contains two actions inside two nouns and no one responsible. Anyone who translates it into plain language writes: 'We are going to review the applications that arrived on time.' The same content, a third of the words and a subject. That translation is the work of C1.

listening.script:
Funcionario: Se denegó la solicitud porque no se aportó la documentación.
Ciudadana: ¿Puede decirlo de otra manera?
Funcionario: Sí: faltaba un papel y por eso no la aceptamos.
Ciudadana: Gracias — así se entiende.
listening.gloss: Officer: The application was refused because the documentation was not provided. Citizen: Can you say it another way? Officer: Yes: a paper was missing and that is why we did not accept it. Citizen: Thanks — that way it is understandable.

mistakes.wrong: Se procederá a revisar las solicitudes, y se procederá a decidir después.
mistakes.right: Se revisarán las solicitudes y se decidirá después.
mistakes.why: Two nominalisations of the same verb are a draft problem, not a register.

mistakes.wrong: El informe fue redactado por mí mismo ayer por la tarde.
mistakes.right: El informe lo redacté yo ayer por la tarde.
mistakes.why: Spanish turns a stiff passive into an active sentence with a pronoun.

mistakes.wrong: Cabe señalar que es necesario que se debe de revisar.
mistakes.why: Stacked periphrases; one modal is enough.

task.title: Un-nominalise one paragraph
task.instructions: Find one paragraph of Spanish administrative or academic prose — a form letter, a handbook page, an abstract — and rewrite it twice: once with the verbs restored and one subject per sentence, once for a reader who has ninety seconds. Then put the original and both versions side by side and mark the nouns that turned back into verbs. That list is the C1 vocabulary.
